owner: ok, this worked, though it seems like the rendezvous target is only available from the initial state of the 'Rendezvous' scenario. if you perturb the manuever too much or delete it and add a new one, the target is greyed out. Which may be by design but it seems like I could make a rendezous trajectory manually but the option to add the correction at the end didn't seem to enable again. A small nit too is that when editing a current trajectory but not actively dragging the control handles, hovering along the estimated path should still scrub the other bodies along with it, so you can better tell what's going on. While there may be something else going on here, in CoaDE when the sim trajectory intersects the sim trajectory of another body, the intersection point also gets marked with an 'match orbit' icon, which when clicked then adds the correction maneuver for that, and then if the phase is close enough also adds a 'intercept' icon to also match velocity. I think that's worth adopting here. Also CoaDE has an affordance that if there's overlapping bodies/markers at the current zoom level/view, clicking on one of the overlapping icons opens a dropdown menu at mouse position that you can select which one you mean, including a "add new manual manuever here" when it's an intercept/match orbit marker, so if for some reason you want that instead of the autopilot, can do that.

chapters.title: Choosing a model train set for spaceships

owner:
cool, I think this largely works as a 2d version of CoaDE's rendezvous. The UI a bit clunky in terms of placing departures; the way that the manuevers also depends on the dock/undock state is hard to keep track of; once we switch to dynamic manuevers we'll have to redesign it anyway though. I think what we'll probably want is the sort of horizontal timeline interface like in opus magnum so you can see linearly what each body is doing. I think it'll also help to have like a timeline of fuel/delta-v remaining over time so you can see where you're using your budget.

The layers control is good; with the bodies only or just the trail it does match the presentation of the transfer orbit wikipedia animations pretty well and I can see it being compelling once we get looping in.

Let's try to plan out how to design the periodic transfer programming in more detail before proceeding, including astra review, and any additional web search to relevant resources from either real space launch planning or other videogames. I don't really have any direct experience with this (CoADE again doesn't really have repeating missions), so I dunno what will fit best, as well as in the terms of how much is calculated for you vs tweaking the manuevers yourself. Some possible links are [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porkchop_plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porkchop_plot) which might be an interesting visualization to show in the game to help pick out schedules. And also [https://www.overvieweffekt.com/tools/brachistochrone-rocket-calculator](https://www.overvieweffekt.com/tools/brachistochrone-rocket-calculator) ; with more realistic deltav budgets, it seems like the puzzles might collapse into mainly hohmann transfers without much room for expression. if we lift the caps beyond chemical propulsion up to constant acceleration, that might make for more interesting design space. Even if that also degenerates where the max-speed solution is straight shots on simple puzzles, I think later puzzles should still have enough complexity where even with torchships they'll be interesting solutions. Plus even with limited budgets, hohmann transfers are also 'straight lines' in a certain sense.
exchanges.summary: Researched periodic mission planning, propulsion regimes, launch-window visualizations and programming-game precedents. Drafted a periodic transfer-programming proposal for outside review.

owner: Hmm, while I still think this is still feasible I'm still not seeing how this works as crisply as I hoped yet. Thinking about the abstract structure of opus magnum or spacechem or infinifactory, it feels different qualitatively than logistics at this level; I don't know exactly how though, but maybe there is some schematic or analytical way to characterize the difference. There's a lot more transformation and spatial constraints, whereas orbital logistics has almost no spatial constraint. I have played a lot of factorio and its train schedules have a similar feel to this as well as the abstractions on top of it like interrupts and mods like logistics train network. I however haven't played other train or transport simulators. https://www.openttd.org/ is open source, I think it might be worth exploring its source for game design space like how it both does schedules and UI and also gameplay justification for those. There's definitely a continuum between zachtronics programming games and factory automation games; I feel like there's maybe some better way to fit the topology of orbital logistics in that continuum than our current path of "cycling machine with orbital transports inside of it". Please do another research and planning round with this in mind.
exchanges.summary: Compared the transformation/spatial constraints of programming puzzles with the scheduling and network constraints of transport games, including OpenTTD and train logistics.

owner: I think it's actually worth spawning an astra sub agent as well, in a less constrained form than the senior review flow, more of a "game design consultant", with access to its own sub agents/ability to run code and do experiments as it sees fit.
exchanges.summary: Ran a less constrained Astra design consultation with numerical experiments and prior-art research. Its conclusions helped separate an enjoyable operating exhibit from a compulsory optimization game.

owner: ok, I think the proposal is sound and correctly identifies the abstract differences between the other game's design space and what we have currently. I'm realizing that my own desiderata for this game's design are slowly drifting higher level from like actually designing the maneuvers with a CoaDE UI of broad changes + solver to generally having the maneuvers calculated for you (i.e. hohmann) but deciding high level on policies for transfers/loading/refuelling . I'm even realizing that at some level I don't even want to design the policies really, and that it'd almost be fine to have like a linear programmer spit out a schedule, but I still want to be able to observe the spaceships moving around (not necessarily as a baked video/gif, a live viewer would be fine too). so the goal could be more like a virtual model train set but for spaceships, and maybe sets for specific proposed plans like the mars cycler, or maybe the NASA artemis proposals with moonbase/station; in the existing demos it's still fun watching the different inertial frames as the animation plays out even when I had no input/just clicked the solve buttons, so that's evidence even minus the game, an interactive/scrubbable n-body simulation might be enough.
exchanges.summary: Reframed the project around watching prepared orbital model sets. A cross-model consultation also examined the appeal of an operating freight exhibit without required authoring.
exchanges.omission: Account and model-CLI setup discussion omitted.

owner:
I agree that the orbital model set viewer is the right next direction vs trying to make a puzzle game. I think unlike nasa eyes I would like to be able to watch fictional space buildups e.g. lots of space stations at various orbits and traffic between them and planet/moon ground stations with simulated cargo loadouts, at various settings like earth/moon, or earth/mars, or jupiter and moons, up to full solar system, and potentially exotic technologies like torchships/solar sails once we move beyond simple impulse particle ships. or potentially fictional or non-sol systems, e.g. traffic in a binary star system with planets would probably be neat. Some other prior art that's sort of like this are existing viewers for all the satellites orbiting earth (communications and others) but that doesn't have the same logistics/orbital transfer appeal, and is way more dense/cloudy than I imagine for spaceships. And unlike something like Universe Sandbox, the focus is on schematic spaceships vs the planetary bodies, and thus various inertial views and potentially things like gravitational potential fields/rubber-sheet view or energy/porkchop plots as simultaneous views are more important than like planet atmosphere or star or ring rendering.

The research from actual model train culture is interesting; I was unaware of their own breakdown of autonomous loops vs operations roleplay. That's probably also relevant for future extensions here, like even if the maneuvers and planning are automated, it'd be interesting to see somewhere in the UI some level of simulation of e.g. space station or planet/asteroid colony needs like stationkeeping fuel and other upkeep, and if they're manufacturing, imports/exports; though going too deep there approaches turning this into into a solar system strategy/expansion game like Solar Expanse; and certainly don't need that in this prototype stage.

So this does mean we can likely retire the maneuver editing UI from CoaDE (at least from this prototype, if we end up wanting it later for sandbox/editors can recover from git history). And with that lifted it's also more feasible to upgrade the project to full 3D; though I think we can still validate a lot of the desiderata in 2D still so I don't think we need to build that and the extra viewer complexity immediately, though it may be worth adding the 3rd coordinate to the simulation engine and and just restrict orbits to in plane, to make sure the simulation/solver parts still work earlier.

With that I think good to continue with implementation here, ask me any clarifying questions if needed.
exchanges.summary: Retired the maneuver editor from the main viewer and built prepared fictional freight exhibits with shared playback, reference frames, ship inspection and activity timelines.

owner:
Nice, I like this a lot. Good validation that this level of interaction is actually what I want vs first having to build maneuvers themselves. The rotating frames are also cool and help build intuition for how e.g. the retrograde orbit looks complex in the primary body frame but actually simple in the rotating frame, or in the logistics case, why the hohmann transfer orbits are efficient. The only real nit I have is when the label layer is enabled, the text labels jump around frame to frame to try to avoid overlap which is distracting; I mostly left them turned off which worked fine; might just need some hysteresis or overlap fade instead (other e.g. map viewer software might have good heuristics for how to choose what to display under dynamic positioning like this)

What do you think is worth building next? I think there are several possibilities here but not sure what to choose yet; since it's late for me I would like something that seems like it could succesfully run autonomously for longer without my feedback to make use of my sleeping hours.

owner:
